stimulus:
Shards (unordered, do not explain them, just let them sit):

– the slime mold abandons the tunnel it just built
– salt crust ringing a dried lake, one ring per drought
– a luthier taps the spruce and listens for where it wants to be thinner
– moth wings: scales arranged so light is lost on purpose
– tide tables kept by a village that has never seen a chart
– the bureaucrat's stamp that makes a thing true
– sourdough starter inherited, never started
– an error bar drawn in charcoal by someone who is tired
– ant bridges made of ants, dissolving downstream
– kintsugi: the fracture becomes the most valuable line
– a negative result mailed in a bottle to the wrong decade
– the rope that is strong only because no fiber runs the whole length
– lichen: two organisms filing one tax return
– a ferry timetable read backwards
– noise as the ingredient, not the contaminant
– the map that is the same size as the territory, folded

Instruction to self: before answering the question that follows, pick two or three shards that feel least related to it. Borrow the underlying mechanism of each (not the imagery). Force each mechanism onto the problem and ask what experiment, measurement, or design it would imply. Prefer ideas that would make a specialist say "odd, but testable" over ideas that would make them say "yes, standard."

Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Rope-fiber test: relay of AP-1 occupancy across short-lived members
ideas.description: Rope strength comes from overlapping fibers, none of which spans the whole length. Test whether memory persists even though no single AP-1 protein or complex persists: use degron-tagged FOS/JUN family members, pulse-label with HaloTag, and run CUT&Tag at timepoints long after a stimulus. If sites stay occupied while the original molecules have turned over, memory is carried by a relay of exchanging subunits and chromatin state. If occupancy requires the original molecules, it is not.

ideas.title: Salt-ring chromatin accessibility record of past stimuli
ideas.description: Each drought leaves its own ring, so the crust is a stack of records. Stimulate cells with repeated, distinct pulses (e.g., TPA, then anisomycin, then serum) and run single-cell ATAC plus AP-1 motif-resolved footprinting. Test whether each stimulus leaves a separable, ordered accessibility signature at AP-1 sites that persists after washout and reads out history. Dropping FOS or JUN acutely, or placing a dominant-negative (A-FOS) after the stimulus, tests whether AP-1 is needed to maintain the record rather than only to write it.

ideas.title: Noise as ingredient: single-cell AP-1 fluctuation spectra predict memory
ideas.description: Treat transcriptional noise as the signal. Live-image an endogenous FOS/JUN reporter (MS2 or knock-in fluorescent tag) in single cells over days and measure the autocorrelation and pulse statistics of AP-1 activity. Test whether cells with higher pulse frequency or longer autocorrelation retain a primed response (faster, stronger re-induction of target genes) on restimulation. Then use optogenetic control of pulse patterns, with the same total dose delivered as bursts or as a plateau, to causally test whether the temporal pattern encodes memory.

ideas.title: Kintsugi perturbation: break AP-1 sites and see whether the scar becomes the memory
ideas.description: The fracture becomes the most valuable line. Use CRISPR to damage individual AP-1 motifs at enhancers, or use CRISPRi/dCas9 to evict AP-1 transiently, in cells with primed enhancers. Then quantify whether repair or recovery leaves a stable epigenetic scar, such as altered H3K27ac, methylation, or reduced re-binding, and whether the response to a second stimulus is changed. Comparing wild-type with a mutated motif and with transient eviction separates sequence-encoded memory from state-encoded memory.

ideas.title: Lichen test: AP-1 and a partner as a joint memory unit
ideas.description: Two organisms filing one return suggests that memory belongs to the pair and not to either partner. Test whether AP-1 memory needs a partner such as a pioneer factor (e.g., ETS, CEBP, or SWI/SNF/BAF). Acutely degrade AP-1 or the partner after priming, and use sequential ChIP or CUT&RUN co-occupancy plus Micro-C to map the joint state. Memory that is lost only when both are present, or only when the partner is removed, would show that AP-1 recruits a memory-bearing complex and does not itself store it.
